newsitem.title: BELGIUM: City Hotels says bond issue 75% bookbuilt.
newsitem.headline: City Hotels says bond issue 75% bookbuilt.

text.p: Victor Hasson, chairman of Belgian hotels and airline group City Hotels, said on Thursday he was confident the company's one billion Belgian franc five-year convertible bond issue would close early on February 17.
He told reporters after a news conference that the book building for the issue already amounted to about 75 percent and that retail investors would easily account for the remainder.
A source close to the deal said Belgian insurance companies were among the institutionals which had already guaranteed bids for the issue.
Suscriptions began on Thursday and will run in theory until February 19. But they can be closed early after three days on February 17, and Hasson told Reuters this would be the case.
Existing shareholders can subscribe at a rate of two bonds for each five shares held in the first three days of the issue.
But City Hotels said in its prospectus that its stable shareholders would not use their preferential rights.

Francis Vanderhoydonck of Generale Bank, which is organising the issue with Banque Degroof, told the news conference that the stable shareholders would refrain from subscribing as the issue was also aimed at broadening the shareholder structure.

But he added that the stable shareholders would help guarantee the issue. The prospectus said that Generale Bank would guarantee the issue for 350 million francs, and stable shareholders for 150 million.

City Hotels, which has launched the issue to raise funds for its hotel business in the United States, said earlier that one warrant was attached to each bond of 5,000 francs. The warrant entitles the holder to subscribe to a new share with a VVPR strip at 5,000 francs.
